column1: #     SLIDES 1-12 STANDING, 18 Aug eve    186 wpm   <- 2514 words in 13:29
# The last is the one to trust: the whole authored deck, standing, in one run.
# 186 wpm, and steady — the per-slide spread is 158 to 212 with one outlier.
#     measured 13:29   against 14:50 of caps for those twelve   -> 1:21 UNDER
# **The planning rate stays 140.** MB, 18 Aug: "we still need a comfortable
# margin for nervosity & interruptions of any kind, so don't take my WPM as the
# target." 186 minus 22% is 145, so 140 remains slightly conservative.
# THREE SLIDES ARE OVER CAP EVEN AT SOLO PACE, and those are the real ones:
# Everything else came in under, several by more than twenty seconds.
# ONE DELIVERY FLAG, not a budget one: 01-title ran 128 words in 27 seconds —
# 284 wpm, on the slide that carries the thesis of the whole talk. Finishing
# early there is not a saving.
# A cap is the AIRTIME a slide gets on the night. It is a pacing decision and
# does NOT move when the planning rate moves — the rate only decides how many
# words fit inside it. Caps total 40:50 against a 45:00 slot.
# `demo` rows score at the lower DEMO_WPM — on a live edit you talk around
# typing and pause while the room reads the error. The four demos are 9:15,
# 20% of the slot, and before these rows existed the tool could not see one
# `stub` rows are v2 slides that do not exist yet, carrying their planned cap
# so `make timing` measures the deck we INTEND rather than the deck we have.
# ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH for durations. The plan quotes this file, never the
# reverse: three drafts running, hand-carried arithmetic in the plan drifted in
# the same direction every time (Part 8/C10, C12).
# Caps rebalanced 18 Aug against MB's measured standing run. Time is moved,
# not shaved (C10): the four slides that came in well under cap give it to the
# three that came in over. Net zero.
# These were `stub` rows until the act was written, and stayed `stub` after it
# was — so `make timing` printed the planned cap and hid the real script. They
# are `prose` now: the act measures long against its caps and the tool has to
# say so, which is the whole point of C10. Cut #5 (merge connectives and
# quantifiers) is the reserve if the read-through confirms it.
# ── Act 2 · Ground floor — 2:20 · all three exist ──────────────────────────
# a2-values and a2-promises are cues + a scripted landing line, so they carry
# an EST-WORDS declaration rather than a countable script (Part 6b/T).
# a2-values CUT 18 Aug (MB): "doesn't really make a coherent or important
# enough point, and doesn't fit in well". Its two load-bearing facts are
# relocated rather than lost — Payment<Initiated> and Payment<Authorized> being
# the same bytes belongs at A3-stage4 where phantom types appear, and the
# affordability argument belongs at A6-cost, which is the cost slide. Its 0:50
# goes to A2-scenario (+0:15) and back to the pool.
# 21-bridge deleted 18 Aug — Part 4 makes it two spoken sentences between
# A3-payoff-bob and A3-stage4; it never earned 1:30 of its own.
